verdicts.note: Two independent recorded votes for new revenue: the 1% levy increase plus banked capacity (Dec. 2, 2025) [S5] and a new 0.1% councilmanic sales tax (Jan. 6, 2026), with his own on-the-record rationale [S6][S7]. That clears the second-source bar for high. +1, not +2: the levy increase is the routine statutory 1% and the sales tax is a flat tax, not the progressive or wealth revenue the pole_b label describes, and he says he dislikes impact fees [S14].

Mixed toward pole_b: public funding through the housing sales tax and mobile-home-park protections [S1][S6], alongside middle-housing and permitting supply measures [S3][S4]. Note that he recused from the moratorium extension vote [S12], so the mobile-home-park claim rests on his own campaign materials.

0 holds. The campaign site literally pairs law-enforcement and justice-system investment and body cameras with 'a balanced approach that addresses both crime and the root causes behind it' and treatment-linked shelter [S3][S4]. The unanimous July 21 vote to send Props 12/13 to voters [S8] is a ballot-placement vote and is correctly not used as safety evidence.

Challenger platform only, but the same explicit position appears in three sources: pamphlet 'tax-last' [S1], website 'Tax increases are too often a short sighted strategy' [S2], and launch statement on 'continuous tax increases' [S3]. Repeated explicit statements meet the guide's high bar. -1 is right; 'tax-last' is not a no-new-taxes pledge.
Repeated explicit statements: 'We must address out of control spending' [S2], reprioritize funding to core services [S3], responsible budgeting before new taxes [S1].

Fee, land-use and permit-path reductions as the housing lever, repeated on the website and in the launch release [S2][S3]. Nothing on tenant protections or public housing either way, so -1 rather than -2.

Treatment-and-accountability framing repeated in three sources [S1][S2][S3], with the explicit rejection of housing-first and harm reduction and support for law enforcement on the website [S2]. 'Compassionate' framing keeps it at -1.
